items.summary: D’Angelis’ maiden flight in 1910 set in motion the aviation history of Madras. From a record-making 27-hour flight from London to Madras in a de-Havilland Dove and a night land that left the pilots “trembling like a leaf” to an air taxi that flew all the way to Burma and Alagappa Chettiar’s Jupiter Airways, the skies above Madras have surely never seen a dull moment

items.title: Getting around Madras on autorickshaws
items.summary: From numbering around 200 in 1973 to around 1 lakh in 2026, autorickshaws in the city have come a long way, but so too has the love-hate relationship the residents share with this ubiquitous mode of transport. But if you are in a hurry, the autorickshaw is your best bet to reach your destination, traffic rule violations and all

items.title: How buses became the lifeline of Madras
items.summary: Packed to the point of tipping over, driven rashly, and battered all over, is how one would describe the MTC buses that ply in the city. While buses were in use in Madras since the 1920s, they really took off only after the tram service met its demise in 1953. Since then, they have become an integral feature of the city and a lifeline for millions

items.title: How bicycles, motorcycles took over the roads of Madras
items.summary: Bicycles first came to Madras sometime in the 1880s, and at the time, they had a modest start, with there even being demands for a separate lane for cyclists. And while cycles were riding onward, two-wheelers of the motor variety, not so quietly, took to the roads. Brands such as Royal Enfield even set up manufacturing units in the region. To this day, two-wheelers number among the most convenient ways for getting around in the city

items.title: Hauling about the Madras city on trains
items.summary: Madras was the first place in India where trains were introduced. In 1856, Royapuram became the terminus for a line that ran to Walajah Road. On the suburban side, the ball began rolling in the 1900s, and while the network grew, it never quite rivalled those in places such as Mumbai. Then came the MRTS, which never realised its full potential. At present, Metro Rail is the city’s latest attempt to get back on track

items.title: When yellow-black taxis cruised the roads of Madras
items.summary: In the 1960s and 1970s, yellow taxis were a force to contend with in Madras. While this mode of transport was never as prolific as its contemporaries, it nonetheless had a presence, with the prepaid taxis at the airport being the chief representative. The yellow-black cab was gradually sidelined by services such as taxis on call and aggregator apps. By 2023, it has been reported that only 304 of them still ride around the city

items.title: The four key roads of Madras that originate from Fort St. George
items.summary: Madras’ traffic movement is by and large planned on a network created by four great roads. Today, we know them as Rajaji Salai, Kamaraj Salai, EVR Periyar Salai, and Anna Salai, and each retaining their distinct identities. However, their focal point to this day remains Fort Saint George

Their role was replaced by the marginally better cycle rickshaw, which received a helping hand from MGR’s 1971 blockbuster Rickshawkaran

items.title: Aboard the tramway in Madras
items.summary: When Madras’ first tramway took to the streets in the 1870s, it was horse-drawn. A little over two decades later, the city got its electric tramway system going, much before any other city in the country. Up until its demise in April 1953, the Madras Electric Tramways Company Limited was largely plagued by malfunctions, never once managing to turn a profit

items.title: Jolted about on carts drawn by oxen and horses in Madras
items.summary: When animal-powered transportation was in its heyday in the Madras region, it came in multiple varieties. While businessmen preferred the fast-moving rekla, which were even used for races, the horse-drawn jhutkas, which became the first public transport of Madras, were in use as recent as 1969. At one point, these carts required a licence and were even exempt from taxes, at least the ones drawn by horses and bullocks

items.title: Masula boats and the fishermen who kept Madras afloat
items.summary: Before the harbour came into being, arriving in Madras by ship meant making the last leg of the journey on masula boats. These boatmen, who were mostly fishermen from the coast along Madras, knew that they were a vital link in keeping the city’s trade alive and made full use of the opportunity. But by the late 1890s, their era had all but come to an end

Even records of The East India Company contain details of hire charges of palanquin bearers, with rates higher than even hiring horses. Nowadays, this yesteryear means of transport is mainly consigned to museums

items.title: Rs 428 crore in, Rs 1 crore out: How Chinese capital and public money vanished into Gurugram’s garbage
items.summary: In 2017, Ecogreen was hired to collect and process garbage in Gurugram and Faridabad, and to reduce the enormous Bandhwari landfill. A Chinese company invested Rs 428 crore in Ecogreen, and the government paid it another Rs 157 crore. But the promised waste-to-energy plant was never built and the landfill grew into a 38-metre-high garbage mountain, polluting the groundwater of nearby villages. Company records show that large sums went to related companies, consultancy fees and advances for machinery that never arrived. In 2024, the government cancelled Ecogreen’s contract and its Chinese owner sold the company for just Rs 1 crore. Ecogreen is only part of a larger problem: waste management in Gurugram has become an endless garbage contract, with one company after another failing to deliver as public spending and garbage pile up. *** Start at the end. In the summer of 2024, a Chinese firm that runs waste-to-energy plants sold its entire Indian business for Rs 1 crore – about the price of a modest flat in the city it had been hired to clean. Seven years earlier it had bought that same business, pumped in roughly Rs 428 crore, and promised to shrink the growing landfills in Gurugram and Faridabad. Somewhere between the Rs 428 crore that went in and the Rs 1 crore that came out is the story of too many backers disappointed. And it is not a simple one, of an Indian company taking foreign investors for a ride. This is the story of that Indian firm, Ecogreen Energy Pvt Ltd, failing to deliver the Indian expansion that China Jinjiang Environment Holding Co Ltd had made it the anchor of. It is the story of a web of firms linked to Ecogreen – some the promoters’ own – in effect absorbing money meant for waste plants and garbage processing into consultancy fees, rent and inside deals. It is the story of the Bandhwari landfill, which the company was hired to shrink, climbing instead towards a mountain taller than the Aravalli slope beside it. Of the processing plant that was to transform the city, and that exists to this day only as a model made of wood and plastic. And it is the story of the bill, which the public paid whether or not anything worked. More than Rs 325 crore of taxpayers’ money went for targets that were barely met. items.title: Better-half will become bitter-half if issues not addressed: Delhi HC acquits man for murder attempt against wife
items.summary: Marriage is paradoxical and a world of extremities, the Delhi High Court recently observed while acquitting a man who was convicted by a trial court for attempting to murder his wife by forcing Baygon Spray (an insecticide) down her throat [Nafe Singh v State] . Justice Vimal Kumar Yadav said that “the best, in no time, becomes worst if not handled carefully”. The Court highlighted recent examples wherein spouses resorted to extreme levels of violence against each other, which was incomprehensible some decades ago. “The better-half becomes the bitter-half if issues are not taken care of and resolved as soon as possible. One of the most beautiful relationships of humans, that is of a husband and wife becomes one of the most terrible when things go wrong in a matrimonial alliance. Time, albeit, is a big healer and tones down a lot of pains in life, however in relationships time taken can also be counterproductive,” the Court stressed. It added that relationships can go in a totally different, undesirable, and unexpected direction if not handled carefully. items.title: Indian courts show no bias against Chinese companies: Senior Advocate Darius Khambata
items.summary: Indian courts do not discriminate against Chinese companies and have granted them relief by enforcing arbitral awards and freezing assets, Senior Advocate Darius Khambata said on Monday. Khambata was speaking at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) Symposium 2026 during a panel titled Cross-Border Disputes across China, India and the US: Strategy, Enforcement and Risk . The session was moderated by Clifford Chance partner Kabir Singh . The other panellists were Three Crowns founding partner Luke Sobota , Alibaba Group’s Head of Dispute Resolution and Regulatory Investigations Li Jieyun and Hui Zhong Law Firm Singapore head Hazel Tang . Khambata said that Indian courts remained fair and agnostic about the nationality of parties appearing before them. “ I don’t see any bias in favour of our nationals against any particular national. Chinese companies have won enforcement of awards. They have won Section 9 interim injunctions to freeze assets in Indian courts. ” Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act allows courts to grant interim protection before, during or after arbitral proceedings. Such relief may include orders preserving disputed property, securing the amount involved in the dispute or preventing a party from disposing of its assets. Khambata said that this approach would continue despite the political tensions between India and China. “That should be so. But, of course, the political tensions are resulting in a complete reduction of trading relationships .” Geopolitical and political considerations were presently overriding the economic potential of the two countries, he added. It will become potentially the greatest trading relationship the world has ever seen .” Khambata also addressed the effect of sanctions and tariffs on international trade and arbitration. items.summary: Weeks after fitness platform Cult.fit filed its draft papers for an initial public offering (IPO), its co-founder Rishabh Telang has moved the Karnataka High Court to quash a criminal case recently lodged against him by his brother-in-law [Rishabh Telang Vs State] Justice M Nagaprasanna on Tuesday issued notice to the State and complainant Deepak Poduval at whose instance the FIR against Telang was lodged. items.title: Allahabad HC asks State to enhance compensation for dependents of advocates under financial aid scheme
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has directed the State government to consider enhancing the amount of compensation payable to the dependents of deceased advocates [ Jyotima v State of UP and 2 Others ]. A Division Bench of Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prashad noted that the compensation under the ‘Financial Assistance Scheme for Advocates’ was fixed at ₹5 lakh in 2015 and since then, the corpus for the scheme has swollen to ₹330 crore from ₹20 crore. However, the Court observed that the compensation amount has remained static at ₹5 lakh. It thus called upon the government to consider increasing the compensation amount. “Let the Government come up with an affidavit as to what amount it proposes to enhance towards the compensation under financial assistance scheme, and we leave it to the wisdom of the State Government. If a proper affidavit in this regard is not filed by the next date fixed, this Court will be compelled to take a serious view of the matter,” the Court directed. Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prashad The Court was hearing a petition moved by a widow of an advocate for payment of interest on account of the delayed disposal of her application seeking compensation of ₹5 lakh. She had applied for compensation in 2020 but the same was paid only in 2025. On July 7, the Court took a serious view of the delay and directed Member Secretary of the Uttar Pradesh Advocate Welfare Fund Trustee Society, Lucknow (trust), to explain the delay in disbursing the compensation to the needy and eligible dependents of deceased advocates. items.title: Delhi HC directs State to decide public prosecutors' challenge to biometric attendance system
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday directed the Delhi government to decide within four weeks the public prosecutors’ plea challenging Aadhaar based biometric attendance system [ Delhi Prosecutors Welfare Association Vs State GNCT of Delhi and Anr ]. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma passed the directions on August 17 while considering a petition filed by Delhi Prosecutors Welfare Association seeking quashing of Delhi government’s circulars requiring recording of biometric attendance of public prosecutors. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma The petitioner-association challenged two circulars mandating the implementation of Aadhaar Enabled Biometric Attendance System (AEBAS) for public prosecutors. The association submitted that public prosecutors, being officers of the court, are required to visit different courts, police stations and other locations while discharging their duties. The biometric system is impractical and the presence of prosecutors is reflected in the court records and proceedings, it was contended. Biometric attendance was implemented without taking into account their previous representation to the government challenging the mechanism, it was submitted. The association alternatively sought a court-centric attendance mechanism keeping in mind the nature of work and duties of public prosecutors. The Court converted the public prosecutors’ plea into a representation to the concerned authorities under Delhi government and directed the State to reach a decision on the issue within four weeks from August 17. “This Court finds it appropriate to direct that the present petition filed before this Court be treated as a representation on behalf of the petitioner, and the respondents are directed to decide the same, within a period of four weeks from date, under intimation to the petitioner herein, after giving a personal hearing to the petitioner,” the Court directed. While disposing of the matter, the Court also granted liberty to the association to approach the court in case of further grievance. Advocates Krishan Kumar, Rajesh Mishra and Anubhav Kumar appeared for the association. Standing Counsel Avnish Ahlawat with advocates Nitesh Kumar Singh, Aliza Alam and Mohnish Sehrawat appeared for Delhi government. [Read Order]

items.title: Law firm name not family property: Calcutta HC bars Somabrata Mandal from claiming connection with Fox & Mandal
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Monday perpetually restrained Somabrata Mandal and his law firm from holding themselves out as being associated with the 130-year-old law firm Fox & Mandal, or from using the marks "Fox & Mandal," "Fox and Mandal," and "F&M." Justice Ravi Krishan Kapur passed a summary judgment on the issue, on a suit filed by Fox & Mandal against Somabrata Mandal and his law firm, “Fox Mandal.” “This is a fit case for summary judgment and the prayer for a decree of perpetual injunction restraining the defendant nos. 1 (Somabrata) and 2 (Fox Mandal), their men, servants, agents and assigns and other partners from holding themselves out in any manner whatsoever as being associated with the plaintiff no. 1 firm (Fox and Mandal) or the plaintiff no. 2 (LLP set up by Fox and Mandal), or claiming any legacy in the year of establishment of the plaintiff no. 1, i.e., 1896, or passing off their firm or their legal services as that of the plaintiff no. 1 or the plaintiff no. 2, and also from using the marks 'Fox & Mandal', 'Fox and Mandal' and 'F&M', is granted,” the Court ruled. Justice Ravi Krishan Kapur The case concerned the goodwill and reputation associated with the law firm Fox and Mandal/ Fox & Mandal. The firm was set up in 1896 as a partnership between an English attorney named John Kerr Fox and an Indian attorney named Gokul Chandra Mandal. The Court noted that it was perhaps the only example of an Indo-British joint venture in the legal profession that has had continuous existence for over 125 years. items.title: Tiger has a place in India’s Constitution and ecological balance: Arjun Ram Meghwal
items.summary: The tiger has a place both in the artwork of India’s original Constitution and in maintaining the country’s ecological balance, Union Minister of State for Law and Justice (Independent Charge) Arjun Ram Meghwal said on Saturday. Meghwal was speaking at the launch of Sacred Tiger Tales: From Vedic Hymns to Tryst with Stripes , authored and photographed by senior Law Ministry official Manoj Kumar. The 248-page coffee-table book, published by OakBridge Publishing, was unveiled by Meghwal alongside Attorney Genera l R Venkataramani at the India International Centre in New Delhi. The book features 82 short narratives spanning scripture, classical literature, folklore, colonial history, and modern conservation, alongside photographs taken across Indian tiger reserves. The launch brought together figures across law, government, wildlife conservation, photography and publishing. Meghwal referred to the artwork in the original handwritten Constitution prepared under the guidance of artist Nandalal Bose, noting that its decorative borders incorporate animal representations including a tiger motif. “The constitutional journey of ‘We, the people of India’ is not separate from nature, ” Meghwal said in Hindi. The Minister also highlighted the artwork accompanying Part XVI of the Constitution, which depicts Rani Lakshmibai and Tipu Sultan, popularly remembered as the “Tiger of Mysore”. These illustrations establish a direct civilisational connection between constitutional governance and nature. “ The Constitution is the principal responsibility of our Law Ministry. That is why Manoj-ji has written this book ,” he said. Sacred tiger tales On the tiger’s broader environmental significance, Meghwal stressed that every species created by nature plays an essential role in preserving natural equilibrium. “ The tiger makes a very important contribution towards maintaining ecological balance, ” he said. He recalled a childhood lesson from his schoolteacher who explained that snakes should not be killed out of fear because they control rodent populations that would otherwise destroy food grains. Attorney General R Venkataramani described the book as an exploration of justice extending beyond the human realm. “ This book is about justice in a different space . I began to talk to each one of the photographs, and that was a great discovery for me, ” he said. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta issued notice on a challenge by the public prosecutor against the observations made by the High Court in its order. items.title: Not essential religious practice: Allahabad High Court rejects Muslim student’s plea to wear hijab in school
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently rejected a Muslim student’s plea seeking directions to allow her to wear a (hijab) headscarf in addition to the uniform prescribed by her school [Sukaina Rizvi v State of UP and Others] In a judgment delivered on August 21, a bench of Justice JJ Munir and Justice Indrajeet Shukla noted that High Courts have been unanimous in their opinion that wearing a headscarf is not essential part of the Islamic faith for a woman. Pertinently, the Court also said that Karnataka High Court’s decision against wearing of hijabs in schools continues to hold the field as the Supreme Court is yet to settle the dispute after a split verdict “In view of the difference of opinion, the matter was directed to be placed before the Hon’ble the Chief Justice for the constitution of an appropriate Bench. There is no authoritative pronouncement as yet by the Supreme Court, finally settling the issue, arising from the judgment of the Karnataka Full Bench. We are of opinion that the Karnataka Full Bench, like the other Courts, is nevertheless persuasive authority of great value and there is no reason for us to take a different view,” it noted. Justice JJ Munir and Justice Indrajeet Shukla The Court refused to accept the petitioner’s argument that wearing a headscarf was an essential religious practice for her. There is no pleading or authoritative religious text or material placed on record, sufficient by itself to establish, that the practice about the obligation to wear a scarf inside the classroom, is obligatory and the non-observance thereof would alter the fundamental character of the petitioner's faith, the Court said. “A claim, placing reliance upon Article 25 of the Constitution, cannot be accepted for the sake of mere assertion, without the necessary factual and legal foundation laid for the purpose. A perusal of the writ petition shows that there are no pleadings to that effect by the petitioner, except that she has been doing it since she was a child and ever-since she joined the School in Class-VI,” the Bench added. The Court further observed that so long as the dress code is uniform, bona fide, non-discriminatory and intended to maintain discipline and institutional identity, the choice of the prescribed uniform primarily lies within the domain of the school. items.title: Madras HC orders probe into Teachers Recruitment Board officials for ignoring Supreme Court ruling
items.summary: The Madras High Court has ordered a probe to identify Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB) officials responsible for ignoring a Supreme Court ruling on how reserved-category backlog vacancies must be filled [ Teachers Recruitment Board v. C Vijayalakshmi and connected cases ]. A Bench of Justices SM Subramaniam and Krishnaswamy Govindarajan directed the TRB Chairperson to conduct an inquiry and identify the officials responsible for failing to implement the Supreme Court’s ruling in State of Tamil Nadu v. K Shobana . The Court added that departmental disciplinary proceedings should be initiated against the officials, if necessary. “ The manner in which the provisional selection list for the post of P.G. Assistant (Economics) was issued shows that the Teachers Recruitment Board had disrespected the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court which is deprecated ,” the Court said. The dispute arose from a 2021 notification issued by the TRB for the recruitment of postgraduate assistant teachers in Economics. The candidates before the Court participated in the recruitment process and were included in the first provisional selection list published on September 14, 2022. However, their names were removed when the TRB issued a second provisional list on October 13, 2022. The candidates challenged the revised list, arguing that the recruitment body had incorrectly applied Section 27(f) of the Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016. The provision deals with vacancies reserved for various communities and the treatment of backlog vacancies. In K Shobana , the Supreme Court held that candidates belonging to reserved categories, who qualify on their own merit, must be placed against General Turn vacancies. Such candidates cannot be pulled down from the general merit list and adjusted against backlog vacancies reserved for their communities. The Supreme Court had clarified that the word “first” in Section 27(f) only requires backlog vacancies to be filled before the current reserved vacancies. It does not mean that backlog vacancies must be filled before completing the General Turn merit list. Therefore, the provision relating to reservation becomes applicable only after candidates selected on merit have been accommodated in the General Turn. The TRB admitted before the High Court that it had not followed the Shobana ruling while preparing the second provisional selection list. items.title: Transgender person moves Kerala High Court alleging denial of entry to Sabarimala
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday sought the State government's response to a plea filed by a transgender devotee alleging denial of permission to enter Sabarimala temple due to her gender [Sathyashri Sharmila Rehemathali v State of Kerala & ors]. A bench of Justice Gopinath P and Justice S Manu issued notice to the State and posed the matter to September 3 for further consideration. Justice Gopinath P and Justice S Manu The petition was filed by Sathyashri Sharmila Rehemathali, who identifies as a transgender woman and claims that she is a devote and a regular pilgrim to Sabarimala. According to the petition, Sharmila reached Pamba on August 20 to get Lord Ayyappa's darshan, after observing the required Vratham and carrying her Irumudi (sacred rituals undertaken by devotees). However, around 3:30 PM, she was stopped during a police inspection near the Pamba Ganapathi Temple and informed that she would not be permitted to proceed uphill because she was a transgender person. As per the petition, officers at the Pamba Police Station told her that the Travancore Devaswom Board had instructed the police not to permit transgender persons to proceed to Sabarimala. Sharmila asked the authorities to show her the written order, circular or notification, imposing such a restriction, but was told that the document could not be shown to her. She further pointed out that she had previously visited the temple on January 3 and April 15, 2026, and had been permitted to complete her pilgrimage and receive darshan. The petitioner therefore approached the Court, challenging the sudden restriction on her entry to the temple solely on account of her transgender identity as arbitrary and unconstitutional. She also relied on Section 3(e) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, which prohibits denial of or unfair treatment in, access to public places and religious institution, stating that the authorities failed to enforce the statutory protections. The petitioner has sought, among other reliefs, permission to undertake the pilgrimage to Sabarimala and offer prayers, besides direction to the state government to disclose and publish any circular or notification that restricts the entry of transgender devotees. items.summary: A court in Kashmir has issued a show-cause notice to a tehsildar asking him to explain why appropriate legal action should not be initiated against him over unauthorised use of a red beacon/warning light and multiple-toned siren on his official vehicle. Special Mobile Magistrate (Traffic) Shabir Ahmad Malik passed the order on an application filed by one Muzaffar Ahmad through advocates Sajad Mohi-ud-din and Haroon Rashid. After examining the application and examining the material placed on record, the Court observed that a prima facie case was made out warranting an inquiry into the factual position. The Court directed SSP Traffic Rural Kashmir to physically inspect the official vehicle belonging to tehsildar Tariq Ahmad Sheikh and ascertain whether his vehicle is fitted with a red/blue beacon light and/or multi-toned siren. The Court further directed that if an unauthorised beacon or multiple-toned siren is found, the inspecting authority shall immediately seize/remove the same and initiate action under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and other relevant law. The applicant alleged that the tehsildar, who is posted in Sopore, was using a red beacon/warning light and multi-toned siren on his official vehicle in violation of Rules 108 and 119 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and relevant notifications. State of Uttar Pradesh , wherein unrestricted use of beacons by public officials was deprecated in the context of curbing VIP culture and maintaining the rule of law. items.title: Court fees should be refunded to litigants whose cases can't be heard: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently observed that litigants are “consumers of justice” and they are entitled to a refund of court fees paid if their case cannot be heard because of maintainability [Murugavel Vs Pichai] A Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and KK Ramakrishnan said that a litigant who mistakenly approaches a court lacking jurisdiction does not receive the service for which the court fee was paid. “Jurist Upendra Baxi would call litigants as consumers of justice. Litigants come to the courts for adjudication of their lis. If the matter could not be taken up for adjudication at all because it was not maintainable in the first instance, the litigant did not receive any service. There has been a failure of consideration and a case for refund stands made out ,” the Court said. Justice GR Swaminathan The Bench made the observation while dealing with an appeal filed by one J Murugavel against an arbitral award passed in October 2024. Murugavel directly challenged the arbitral award before the High Court under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. However, the Court noted that Section 37 only provides for appeals against specified orders and does not permit a direct appeal against a final arbitral award. Such an award can only be challenged through a petition under Section 34 of the Act, the Court explained. “ Unfortunately, this appeal came to be filed and what is worse, it was numbered also ,” the Bench remarked while closing the appeal as not maintainable. Murugavel’s counsel then requested that the court fee paid for filing the appeal be refunded. The Court examined Section 70 of the Tamil Nadu Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955, which states that a fee paid by mistake or inadvertence “shall” be refunded. It concluded that the filing of the appeal arose from a failure to properly understand the scope of Section 37 and therefore, amounted to inadvertence. The Court clarified that inadvertence could include ignorance of the law. The Bench also said that a court fee could not be retained when the court was legally incapable of granting the relief sought. Since an appeal against the final arbitral award did not lie under Section 37, acceptance of the court fee for such an appeal was without the authority of law, it added. “ If refund is not ordered, there would be unjust enrichment for the State ,” the judgment stated. items.title: MP/MLA endorsement for women to get ₹2,500 financial assistance a policy decision, did not "come out of sky: Delhi govt to HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday said that it could declare the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana arbitrary if even one deserving woman is excluded from the scheme because of lack of endorsement from the local Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) or the Member of Parliament (MP). Under the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana, the Delhi government provides financial assistance of ₹2,500 per month to eligible women. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia today questioned the rationale behind the condition requiring MP or MLA endorsement. “What is the objective you are trying to achieve by this? Suppose you don’t know any MP or MLA? If even one person is left out [because of the condition], then the scheme is arbitrary. What is the objective you are trying to achieve through this condition? There are thousands of ways you can identify people,” the Bench remarked. Delhi High Court If even one person is left out [because of the condition], then the scheme is arbitrary. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma appeared for the Delhi government and stated that the government took the policy decision to introduce the condition to ensure that no persona non grata (unwelcome person) gets the benefit. Sharma said that the government wants to file a reply in the case and that over six lakh people have received the benefit under the scheme. “Your lordships may not agree with us, but we are entitled to say how the cabinet has seen it and what the position is in other States. This has not come out of the sky. There is something we want to place on record, we will do it,” he said. The High Court said that the wisdom of the government has to be tested on the fundamental rights under the Constitution. It added that there are many other means to ascertain that a persona non grata does not get the benefit. “Wisdom of the government has to be tested on Part 3 [of the Constitution. You can’t go away by saying this. Every decision, Mr Sharma, has to go the test of Part III (of the Constitution),” the Court said. Sharma replied that the government was not "going away" from the issue and that it will file a reply. The Court has now given the government 10 days to file its affidavit, explaining the rationale behind the condition. items.title: Google-Adani data centre will not affect environment: Andhra Pradesh government tells High Court
items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government on Monday told the Andhra Pradesh High Court that it is taking every step to ensure that the construction of the proposed Google-Adani data centres in Vishakapatnam does not affect the environment [ Bolisetty Satyanarayana v. The State of Andhra Pradesh ]. The counsel representing the State government made the submission before a bench of Chief Justice Lisa Gill and Justice Challa Gunaranjan in response to a public interest litigation (PIL) petition raising several concerns about the multi-billion-dollar project, including its potential impact on the environment. " Counsel for the State submits that care and caution is being exercised in ensuring that all steps are taken within the parameters of law and due care is being taken for protection of the environment ," the Court recorded in the order passed after the hearing today. Apart from environmental concerns, the PIL filed by environmental activist and Jal Biradari National Convenor Bolisetty Satyanarayana contended that 160 acres of the land allotted for data centres was temple land which belongs to the Simhachalam Devasthanam. The same should not have been transferred for commercial purposes and ought to be restored to the temple, the petitioner contended. He also argued that while the government has been claiming that the project would strengthen India's digital economy, the data centres will not be storing or processing Indian data. The petitioner also submitted that there was a forest and a water reservoir right next to the site for the data centres. Both are ecologically sensitive locations and construction could cause irreversible damage to ecological balance and biodiversity in the area, it was argued. He further submitted that Visakhapatnam has been suffering major water crises since 2015 and construction of these data centres would only exacerbate the situation. Despite these concerns, the government had not done any environmental impact studies, the PIL petitioner argued. The Court should issue directions to halt further construction until comprehensive studies are undertaken, it was submitted. The PIL will be heard again next week by which time the State government and its various authorities are expected to file their respective counter-affidavits. items.title: Karnataka HC rejects State's plea to cancel bail granted to BJP MLA Byrathi Basavaraj in murder case
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Monday dismissed the State government's petition seeking cancellation of bail granted to BJP MLA Byrathi Basavaraj, who is an accused in the murder of rowdy-sheeter Shivaprakash alias Biklu Shiva [State of Karnataka v. The complaint was lodged by Vijay Lakshmi, the mother of the deceased. According to the complaint, Shiva was attacked at around 8 pm by around 8-9 unidentified persons. The incident was allegedly witnessed by two persons, following which the complaint was registered and a first information report (FIR) was lodged. The investigation was initially conducted by the Bharati Nagar Police and was subsequently transferred to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) pursuant to a State government order. After taking over the investigation, the CID sought permission to invoke provisions of the Karnataka Control of Organised Crime Act (KCOCA) in the case. The competent authority granted permission for invoking the provisions on August 2, 2025. Basavaraj challenged the invocation of KCOCA, which was subsequently allowed by the High Court by an order dated December 19, 2025. Following the rejection of his anticipatory bail plea, Basavaraj was arrested by the CID on February 12, 2026. He was initially remanded to police custody for one week and was thereafter remanded to judicial custody. In February, Basavaraj had approached the Supreme Court seeking anticipatory bail, to no avail. The trial court later granted bail on the ground that the material cited against Basavaraj did not appear to be strong . The trial court also said that it was not necessary to remand him for further custodial interrogation. items.title: Gauhati High Court closes PIL on adjournment reforms after HC notification addresses concerns
items.summary: The Gauhati High Court recently closed a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed seeking uniform guidelines on adjournments and mandatory digital upload of court records. A Division Bench of Justices Michael Zothankhuma and Arun Dev Choudhury on August 10 noted that the petitioner himself submitted that an intervening administrative notification issued by the High Court Registry had addressed the concerns raised in the matter. "Mr. R. Singh, petitioner-in-person submits that in view of the Notification No. 21 dated 23.03.2026, issued by the Registrar General, Gauhati High Court, nothing survives to be adjudicated in the present Public Interest Litigation (PIL). Accordingly, the instant PIL stands closed," the Court said. Justice Michael Zothankhuma Reetam Singh, an advocate enrolled with the Bar Council of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim, had filed the PIL in 2024. He cited his own experience in a case filed under the Negotiable Instruments Act and a money suit to argue that adjournments were being routinely granted by trial courts on inadequate grounds. This violated the scheme of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), and of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC), he contended. He sought directions for a strict adjournment regime limiting adjournments to rare, substantiated circumstances, imposition of costs on counsel seeking unjustified adjournments, a uniform date-allocation system across subordinate courts on the pattern followed by the High Court, and the mandatory online upload of daily order sheets. items.title: Supreme Court restores Congress leader’s election petition challenging BJP MP Kripanath Mallah’s 2024 poll win
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday set aside the Gauhati High Court’s dismissal of an election petition challenging Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Member of Parliament Kripanath Mallah’s victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. [ Hafiz Rashid Ahmed Choudhury v. Kripanath Mallah and Others ] Congress candidate and Senior Advocate Hafiz Rashid Ahmed Choudhury had challenged Mallah's election on the ground that the BJP leader had employed corrupt practices to win the elections from Assam's Karimganj parliamentary constituency. In April 2025, however, the Gauhati High Court, dismissed Choudhury's petition on noting certain defects in it. The High Court did not go into the merits of the case. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran today allowed Chowdhury's appeal against this ruling. The top court held that the defects cited by the High Court to dismiss Chowdhury's petition at the threshold were not fatal. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The defect flagged by the High Court concerned a Form 25 affidavit filed by Choudhury in support of his allegations that Mallah had committed corrupt practices. The original affidavit in the High Court’s record appeared to have been affirmed before a commissioner of affidavits. However, the copy served on Mallah did not carry any endorsement showing such affirmation. The top court today held that this omission did not justify dismissing the entire election petition. " Obviously, the defect under Section 83 does not entail peremptory dismissal under Section 86 of the RoP Act ,” the Supreme Court said. Therefore, it directed the High Court to verify whether the original affidavit contained the required attestation. If it did, the High Court was directed to consider the petition on merits, including by examining the allegations of corrupt practices. If the required attestation was absent, the Court said Choudhury should not be permitted to pursue the allegations of corrupt practices. However, the High Court must still examine other independent grounds, if any, raised in the petition, the Supreme Court added. “ Suffice it to request the High Court to verify and if due attestation of the affirmation on oath is available, proceed with the matter on merits and if not available, not to permit the allegation of corrupt practices to be urged and proceed with the consideration on the merits of the other grounds, if any are pleaded ,” the Court said. Mallah had defeated Choudhury by 18,360 votes, a margin of around 1.

items.title: Forensic evidence should aid cases, not create more burden for survivors: Ex-ASG Pinky Anand
items.summary: Better forensic practices should strengthen cases before courts without creating an additional burden of proof for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, former Additional Solicitor General of India Pinky Anand said at a training workshop in Goa on Saturday. The day-long workshop, held on August 22, focused on implementing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the collection, preservation, chain of custody and presentation of forensic evidence in cases of sexual assault, rape and child abuse. “Better forensic practice must strengthen the case that reaches the court. It must never become a fresh threshold of belief that survivors are asked to clear,” said Anand. The SOPs were formally launched by Anand at the Police Headquarters in Panjim on April 26 last year, marking World DNA Day. They were subsequently expanded to include the handling of forensic evidence in cases involving child abuse. The workshop brought together police officers, prosecutors, judicial officers, medical practitioners and other professionals involved in the investigation and prosecution of sexual and gender-based violence and child abuse cases. A key focus was a victim-centred approach to investigation. The participants discussed how survivors could be treated with dignity and sensitivity while ensuring that evidence is collected in accordance with due process. The sessions also covered practical aspects of collecting and preserving forensic material, maintaining its chain of custody and presenting it before courts. Medical experts discussed factors affecting the reliability and evidentiary value of forensic material. Legal practitioners examined how such evidence should be presented in court. SOP Training Workshop, Goa Speaking at the workshop, Anand said forensic evidence in sexual violence cases can disappear within hours. She cited instances where a survivor may bathe, clothes may be washed or a crime scene may be cleaned. She stressed that procedural discipline was critical to ensuring forensic evidence could withstand scrutiny in court. " The science was sound throughout; what failed, for a time, was the discipline around it — which is precisely what a Standard Operating Procedure exists to secure, from the first responder at the scene to an unbroken chain of custody that can withstand cross-examination," said Anand. items.title: Allahabad High Court takes serious note of IAS officer's alleged attempt to influence trial judge

items.title: Karnataka High Court stays proceedings against man accused of ghosting, seen-zoning his partner
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently stayed criminal proceedings against a man accused of sex on the false promise of marriage after ghosting and 'seen-zoning' his partner [Thufail Ahmed v. State] . Justice M Nagaprasanna observed that the petitioner's conduct did not fulfil the ingredients of Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. "It is the allegation that the petitioner had begun to seenzone the respondent and ghost her throughout. Therefore, the offence under s.69 has sprung. Except this there is nothing else that could become the ingredients of the offence under s.69. In that light there shall be an interim order of stay on further proceedings qua the petitioner till the next date of hearing." Justice M Nagaprasanna Both parties were in a relationship since December 2025. The petitioner told his then partner that he was visiting Chennai, where ailing father was undergoing treatment. Tejpal's appeal was listed before Justice Alok Aradhe today, in the chamber list in which matters are sometimes taken up for preliminary or procedural considerations before it is listed before a regular Bench. Justice Alok Aradhe Representing the Goa government, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta submitted, "Existence of the appeal is dependent on either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, he will have to pray to Your Lordships to allow an exemption from surrendering. These are the two options. My respectful submission is, look at the seriousness of the matter." Tushar Mehta Representing Tejpal, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal countered that there was no need to surrender yet since the High Court itself had granted Tejpal time to surrender. "This rule doesn’t apply because this is a case where stay has been granted by the High Court, so there is no question of applying this rule. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal Notably, on a request by Tejpal, the High Court, in its August 6 verdict, had granted him four weeks to surrender before the jail authorities, although it rejected his plea to stay the conviction. items.title: Supreme Court stays BCI order debarring former judicial officer from legal practice
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday stayed a Bar Council of India (BCI) order permanently debarring a Madhya Pradesh-based advocate, Narendra Kumar Jain from practising law. Jain had earlier served as a judicial officer before resigning from the post [ Narendra Kumar Jain v. Bar Council of India ]. The BCI had passed an order in July, debarring Jain from practice over allegations of professional misconduct arising from repeated, persistent, and unprovoked public attacks on the judiciary and individual judges. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta today sought the BCI's response to Jain's plea and stayed the debarrment order for now. "Issue notice. items.title: Sex between spouses after separation does not condone matrimonial cruelty: Calcutta High Court
items.summary: Stray instances of sexual intercourse between spouses after their separation do not, by themselves, establish that earlier acts of matrimonial cruelty were condoned, the Calcutta High Court recently held. A Division Bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Supratim Bhattacharya made the observation while upholding a decree of divorce granted to a husband on the ground of mental cruelty. The Court said, “ Stray instances of sexual intercourse after separation cannot tantamount to condonation of cruelty per se .” The couple married under the Special Marriage Act on June 18, 2009 and had a child in April 2013. They separated in 2014 after matrimonial disputes arose. The husband subsequently approached a family court seeking divorce on the ground of mental cruelty. The husband alleged that the wife repeatedly made false accusations against him and his family, filed criminal complaints and insisted that he live separately from his dependent widowed mother. A Division Bench of Justice Saumitra Dayal Singh and Justice Swarupama Chaturvedi declared Sections 8, 9, 10, 38 and 42 of the Act ultra vires. The Court held that Sections 8, 9 and 10 – which pertain to payment of rent and its revision - were repugnant to the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. “As to the rent payable, Section 8 allows that revision of the same in terms of Section 9 and for its determination in terms of Section 10. First, revision may arise in terms of the tenancy agreement as may also the case under TPA, but then provisions exist under the Impugned Act to provide for upward revision of the rent at specified rates. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday asked Tamil Nadu government to approach the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) with its grievance that Karnataka was not releasing the State’s proportionate share of Cauvery water. A Bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta was hearing the Tamil Nadu government's plea seeking directions to Karnataka for immediate release of its due share of water. Appearing for Tamil Nadu, the counsel submitted, "We have to receive proportionate quantity or water, that is unfortunately not happening." The Court noted that it had previously observed that Tamil Nadu appeared to have received more water than its allocated share from Karnataka. Today, it pointed out that the State had already received water in accordance with the CWMA's directions. “You have already received the water as directed by CWMA,” said the Court. However, the counsel for Tamil Nadu contended that the CWMA had not directed the release of the proportionate quantity of water that the State was required to receive. The Court then asked Tamil Nadu to approach the CWMA on the issue. The matter will be heard again on August 31. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over Cauvery water dates back to two agreements in 1892 and 1924 between the erstwhile Madras Presidency and the Princely State of Mysore. After several rounds of failed negotiations, the Supreme Court directed the constitution of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, which gave its award in 2007, allowing Tamil Nadu to draw a fixed amount of water every day. However, the dispute continued after both States filed petitions to review the decision. In 2016, Tamil Nadu again petitioned the Supreme Court as Karnataka submitted that it had no more water to share from its reservoir. Subsequently, the top court had asked the Central government to constitute a Cauvery Management Board (CMB). In 2023, the Court declined to entertain an application by the Tamil Nadu government to increase its current share of Cauvery river water from 5,000 to 7,200 cusecs (cubic feet per second) per day. The two States have another water-sharing dispute pending before the apex court. That case concerns the Pennaiyar river . The Tamil Nadu government has filed an original suit in the matter against the Karnataka government and the Central government. items.title: Supreme Court bans construction activities within 100 meters of Rajasthan's Jojari River
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday banned all construction and development activities within 100 metres from the edge of Rajasthan's Jojari River till the conclusion of scientific determination and demarcation of the high flood line and ecological buffer zones [ In Re: 2 Million Lives At Risk, Contamination In Jojari River, Rajasthan ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta passed the order in a suo motu case concerning industrial pollution of rivers in Rajasthan, including the Jojari River. " We are of the considered view that it is necessary to put in place an interim, definite and measurable area of protection so as to adequately safeguard the riverine ecosystem during the pendency of the scientific exercise for the determination and demarcation of the high flood line and the requisite ecological buffer zones. Hence, we hereby direct that no construction or development activity of any nature whatsoever shall be permitted within a distance of 100 meters from the edge of the river in accordance with the aforesaid guidelines," the Court ordered. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta As an additional interim safeguard, the Court also ordered that no hazardous industry or polluting activity shall be permitted within 500 meters on either side of the existing flood line, wherever such flood line has been identified, or the present flow path of the river. The Court said that this arrangement will continue till the high flood line and requisite ecological buffer zones near the river are scientifically determined. The suo motu case before the Court arose after a documentary, "2 Million Lives at Risk | India's Deadliest River | Jojari, Rajasthan," exposed severe contamination in Jodhpur, Pali and Barmer districts. In November 2025, the Court revived the National Green Tribunal's 2022 clean-up directions for the Jojari, Bandi and Luni rivers and set up a high-level ecosystem oversight committee headed by former Rajasthan High Court judge Justice Sangeet Lodha. The Court has since been monitoring industrial pollution and degradation of water bodies in Rajasthan with the assistance of the committee. items.title: TMC MP Mahua Moitra moves Supreme Court against her eviction from Krishnanagar Circuit House
items.summary: Trinamool Congress Member of Parliament (MP) Mahua Moitra has approached the Supreme Court alleging that the Nadia district administration in West Bengal evicted her from her official constituency accommodation at Circuit House in the district in violation of court orders. She told the Court that local officials evicted her from her constituency accommodation in the middle of the night despite a protective High Court order. The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana for urgent listing. "May I mention an Article 32 petition by a sitting lady Member of Parliament who was evicted from her constituency accommodation by local officials, the Additional District Magistrate and the District Magistrate, in the dead of the night at 11 pm. This requires, in our respectful submission, some comprehensive directions because it involves issues of federalism. It also requires an independent investigation. This has happened despite the High Court already having passed a protective order. I am only praying for listing on an early date because this involves an important constitutional issue," the counsel for Moitra said. "We will see," the CJI replied. Moitra moved into the Circuit House after the parliament session in Delhi concluded. She has reportedly alleged that the district administration there has been threatening and harassing her continuously to move out of the Circuit House. items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court is slated to examine whether India's new criminal laws - which took effect from July 1, 2024 - can be applied to a criminal case concerning an offence that took place before 2024, but in respect of which a complaint was filed only in 2025 [ Preeti Dubey v. Vinus Sharma ]. Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal on August 3, sought the assistance of a Senior Additional Advocate General in the matter. The case involves a question of whether the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 - which replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) with effect from July 1, 2024 - would be applicable to a criminal complaint arising from an offence committed before the new criminal laws came into force. “ Since an important question of law has been raised in the instant matter, this Court, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, deems it appropriate to request Ms. Monika Kohli, learned Senior AAG, to render valuable assistance in the instant matter with a view to appreciate the controversy in question," the High Court said. According to the petition, an allegedly defamatory episode took place in 2023, when the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860 and Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973 were in force. The complainant subsequently approached the trial court in January 2025 with a complaint, alleging the commission of offences under Sections 488 (using a false or counterfeit property mark) and 500 (defamation) of the IPC (now replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023/ BNS). The trial court proceeded to consider the case under the BNSS, 2023, and later dismissed an application seeking continuation of the proceedings under the CrPC, 1973. This has been challenged by the complainant (petitioner) before the High Court. items.title: Mockery of Supreme Court order: Karnataka High Court directs State wide audit of CCTV in police stations
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently took strong exception to the State government's argument that CCTV cameras at a police station in Bengaluru were not working due to power outage and lack of back up power [V Shailaja v The Commissioner] . Justice Suraj Govindaraj said that such a stance amounted to mockery of the Supreme Court' s 2020 order to install CCTV cameras in all police stations. "Mockery of the Supreme Court order..What to do? This is a mockery of the order and you submit a report that you complied (with the Supreme Court order). There's an affidavit filed in Supreme Court that every police station has CCTV cameras, fully functional 24 hours. The only conclusion we can arrive at is that you were also happy with it not working; that is why you did not do anything for 1.5 years, it served your purpose. There is no other conclusion that we can draw," the Court remarked. The very purpose of installing CCTV cameras in police stations is defeated if the systems are allowed to remain non-functional during power outages, the bench said. "This will not only affect them but everybody else because if that is the status of CCTV across the State. Then as we said earlier, it is a mockery of the Supreme Court order," the judge remarked. The Court made the observation on August 13 while directing the State authorities to conduct a detailed audit of CCTV systems and power backup infrastructure across all police stations in Karnataka. "We will ask the Home Secretary to look into this and file a detailed report and what steps are to be taken for this," the Court said. Pertinently, the Court directed the Home Department and Police Computer Wing to design, develop and implement a State-level IT system to monitor the functioning of CCTVs in all police stations. items.title: DD News promoted E20 using seven pro-govt farmer leaders without disclosing their ties
items.summary: A nationwide debate is raging over ethanol-blended petrol, or E20, with motorists complaining of lower mileage and alleged engine damage. The government, meanwhile, has stuck to a central defence: E20 is good for farmers. DD News has been an enthusiastic vehicle for that message. Since May, the public broadcaster has aired more than 50 explainers, debates and ground reports promoting E20. But last month, it went a step further, publishing videos of seven farmer leaders on its official social media accounts, all making essentially the same case: ethanol blending is driving farmers’ progress. There was something else these seven had in common. All were already supporters of the Modi government and its policies. Several had backed the three farm laws at the centre of the 2020–21 farmers’ protest, and some had openly opposed the agitation. So, in other words, as criticism of E20 mounted, DD News turned to seven farmer leaders with established pro-government positions to bolster its case for ethanol blending, without disclosing those affiliations to its audience. The seven were K P Singh Thainuan of Gaon Kisan Unnayan, Ashok Balyan of the Peasant Welfare Association, Krishanveer Chaudhary of the Bharatiya Krishak Samaj, Dharmendra Chaudhary of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (Chaudhary Charan Singh), Rampal Jat of the Kisan Mahapanchayat, K Sai Reddy of the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, and Vinod Anand, a member of the government’s MSP committee. All seven videos were published back-to-back on the DD News YouTube channel on July 28, and the messaging across them was strikingly uniform, framing dissent itself as unpatriotic. ‘Anti-national’ Krishanveer Chaudhary called opponents of ethanol blending “anti-national,” saying farmers were shifting from being annadata , or food providers, to urjadata , or energy providers, and that “opposing it cannot be justified in any way”. K P Singh Thainuan dismissed concerns as “entirely baseless” and tied ethanol expansion to the government’s “Viksit Bharat 2047” vision. Ashok Balyan claimed sugarcane, paddy, and maize farmers were benefiting substantially. items.title: Datura sold as food online: Karnataka suspends Amazon, Swiggy, BigBasket licences
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration Department has suspended the food licences of Amazon, Swiggy Instamart and BigBasket until further orders after toxic Datura fruits and seeds were found being sold online as food products. According to an order issued by Food Safety Commissioner K Srinivas, the department has also directed the three platforms to immediately remove listings and advertisements for Datura, also known as Dhatura, and stop selling or distributing the products for human consumption. Datura, known as jimsonweed or devil’s trumpet, is a highly poisonous plant. It is traditionally used in religious rituals, ornamental gardening and some Ayurvedic practices. The entire plant, including its fruits and seeds, is toxic and can cause severe poisoning and death if consumed. Extremely diluted mixtures of the plant are used in Ayurvedic medicines for various purposes. The action followed inspections by food safety officials, who found Datura fruits and seeds being stored and offered for sale through e-commerce platforms using Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) registration or licence numbers. Officials said Datura is poisonous and that its sale or distribution as a food product poses a serious public health risk. During inspections, officials found packets of Datura fruits and seeds carrying food registration numbers. The products were also found stored in a warehouse and listed for sale or distribution through online platforms. The department said collecting, selling or distributing Datura fruits or seeds as food was unlawful given their poisonous nature. The action has been initiated under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. Representatives of the three companies appeared before the adjudicating authority on Monday, August 24, according to the Commissioner's order. Amazon did not submit a response to the notice, while Swiggy Instamart sought more time to submit documents detailing the action it had taken after receiving the department's notice. BigBasket told the authority that it had stopped selling Datura and changed the manner in which the product would be sold. It also said its labelling would be changed to clearly state that the product was “not for human consumption”. The Kerala High Court on Monday, August 24, sought responses from the state government and other authorities on a plea by a transgender woman who alleged that she was stopped from proceeding to the Sabarimala temple because of her gender identity. A Division Bench of Justices P Gopinath and S Manu issued notice to the State, the Pathanamthitta District Collector, Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) and Sabarimala thantri. The matter has been posted for further hearing on September 3. The petition was filed by Sathyashri Sharmila Rehemathali, who identifies as a transgender woman and says she is a regular Sabarimala pilgrim. According to her petition, Sharmila reached Pamba on August 20 after observing the 41-day Mandala Vratham and carrying out the rituals associated with the pilgrimage. However, she was stopped by police near the Pamba Ganapathi Temple and told that she would not be allowed to proceed to the Sabarimala shrine because she was a transgender person. The petitioner alleged that officers at the Pamba police station told her that the TDB had instructed the police not to allow transgender persons to proceed to Sabarimala. When she asked to see the written order, circular or notification imposing such a restriction, she was allegedly told that it could not be shown to her. Sharmila has argued that there is no statutory provision or notified order prohibiting transgender devotees from undertaking the pilgrimage. She contended that, in the absence of a lawful restriction, she could not be denied access to the shrine solely based on her gender identity. She also pointed out that she had previously undertaken the pilgrimage and had darshan at Sabarimala on January 3 and April 15 this year, both before and after her gender transition. The petition relies on Section 3(e) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, which prohibits discrimination against transgender persons in access to public places and religious institutions. items.title: Bengaluru parking fee should not burden residents, says Minister Ramalinga Reddy
items.summary: Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister Ramalinga Reddy has asked Chief Minister DK Shivakumar to reconsider the proposed annual fee of Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 for residential roadside parking in Bengaluru, warning that the charge could put an additional financial burden on middle-class households. In a letter to Shivakumar, Reddy acknowledged the need to crack down on illegal and prolonged parking on city streets, but said the proposed fee should take into account residents who have no alternative parking space within their homes. He pointed out that many families living in older layouts and smaller houses do not have internal parking facilities and are therefore dependent on roadside parking. He also flagged concerns over residents of rented houses and apartment complexes who may face difficulties under the proposed system. Reddy said the additional annual charge would come at a time when households were already dealing with rising living costs and financial commitments such as education, healthcare, vehicle loans and other expenses. "An annual fee of Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 is likely to become another burden," he said in his letter, while urging the government to distinguish between illegal or long-term parking and residents who regularly use their vehicles but do not have parking space at home. The proposed fee is part of the Greater Bengaluru Authority's draft parking regulations, which seek to overhaul parking management in the city and curb congestion caused by vehicles parked on roads for extended periods. The residential parking provision, however, has drawn criticism from residents and others concerned about its impact on households without private parking. Reddy has now urged the Chief Minister to hold consultations with Bengaluru MLAs, resident welfare associations and other stakeholders before finalising the rules. He suggested that the government consider exemptions for residents who genuinely lack access to parking within their premises. "It is important to regulate illegal parking for longer durations. However, an exception should be made to accommodate those who use the vehicles regularly and do not have parking space inside," Reddy said. Sharing his letter on social media, Reddy said the proposed Rs 15,000-Rs 25,000 annual charge needed a "comprehensive review in the public interest". items.title: Karnataka SIR draft rolls are out: What voters need to do next
items.summary: The draft electoral rolls for Karnataka were published on Monday, August 24, marking the next phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the state's voter list. Voters have until September 23 to file claims and objections but even after that window shuts, the process isn't final: people whose claims are rejected can apply again under Form 6, according to Karnataka’s Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukumar. The draft roll contains 4.46 crore electors, compared with 5.54 crore electors on the roll as of June 16. More than 1.07 crore electors from the earlier roll have not been included in the draft and have instead been placed under the Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate or Others (ASDDO) category during the enumeration exercise. However, being left out of the draft roll does not mean that a voter's name has been permanently deleted. The Election Commission has opened a claims and objections period from August 24 to September 23, during which eligible electors can seek inclusion, correct their details or object to wrongful inclusions. Here is what voters need to do next: The first step is to check whether your name appears in the draft electoral roll and whether your details are correct. The draft rolls are available through the Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka, website, the Election Commission's voter services portal and the ECINET mobile application. Citizens can also inspect the rolls at the offices of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) and designated local offices. Booth-wise lists of electors whose names have not appeared in the draft roll after being classified under ASDDO, along with the probable reasons for their non-inclusion, have also been made available through EROs and the CEO Karnataka website. If your name is in the draft roll, check details such as your name, gender, date of birth or age and address. Corrections in case of errors can be made using Form 8. What if your name is missing? If you were on the earlier electoral roll but your name is missing from the draft, you can submit a claim for inclusion during the claims and objections period. This can be done using Form 6.
